chunks: And what is most of the people, even if you wished [eagerly], [would not be] believers.
ai.seo_question: Why do most people not believe despite the Prophet's eagerness?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited in Shia exegesis to illustrate the inevitability of divine decree (Qadr) regarding faith, emphasizes that the Prophet's intense longing (haras) cannot override the collective free will of humanity. It serves as a comfort to the Prophet and believers, clarifying that guidance is ultimately a divine gift rather than solely dependent on human effort, a theme resonating with the concept of 'Amr bayn al-amrayn'.
